### Published articles

#### How to make a payment API safe to retry: idempotency keys, done properly in Go
URL: https://meetjain.xyz/writing/payment-api-idempotency
Published: 2026-07-17
Topics: payment API idempotency, idempotency keys, Go, duplicate charge prevention, PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT, 409 in-progress, request fingerprinting, crash recovery, exponential backoff
Summary: Step-by-step build-along for a Go payment endpoint safe to retry. Covers client-generated idempotency keys (v4 UUID), why lookup-then-write races cause double charges, atomic key claims with PRIMARY KEY + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, three states (new / in_progress / completed), request fingerprint mismatch (422), when not to consume keys (auth/validation), staged crash recovery with payment-rail dedupe, and client retry with backoff+jitter. Includes a production checklist.
Canonical definition — idempotency key: A client-supplied opaque header value that names one operation; identical on every retry of that operation, unique per distinct operation. The server uses it to deduplicate creates and money movements.
